Name: Saurianne's Endemic Echoes
Author: saurianne
Description:
Something I made to get back into the swing of modding, four new barn animals.

The animals here are all irl recently-extinct species of wild animals (meaning they were all Holocene extinctions; the most recent of these went extinct ~130 years ago, and the least recent thousands of years ago), native to various islands around the world:

[list]
[*]The [b]Rodrigues Saddlebacked Tortoise [/b]([i]Cylindraspis vosmaeri[/i]) was one of two giant tortoises endemic to the island of Rodrigues in the Indian Ocean. Its extinction around 1800 was caused in large part by sailors exploiting them for meat and introduced species eating their eggs and young. A major ecosystem engineer, in modern times the related Aldabra tortoise has been introduced to Rodrigues to fill the niche they left empty. As for the Stardew version, it produces tortoise eggs in the fall.[/*]
[*][b]Law's Diving Goose [/b]([i]Chendytes lawi[/i]) was, despite the name, a giant marine duck native to what is now Southern California, which nested on the Channel Islands just off the coast. It went extinct sometime around 800-250 BCE, after surviving about 8,000 years as a food source for the resident humans. Despite a marine diving lifestyle very similar to modern seaducks, [i]Chendytes[/i] was most closely related to modern dabbling ducks such as the mallard. This version produces eggs in the spring.[/*]
[*]The [b]Malagasy Hippoptamus[/b] was a pygmy hippo endemic to Madagascar. There were three known hippo species on the island; this one reflects the most terrestrial, [i]Hippopotamus madagascariensis[/i] (note this genus placement is contested). While they seem to have gone extinct about 1,000 years ago, Malagasy folktales of very similar creatures persist and have led some to suspect the Malagasy hippos may have survived longer than the fossil record indicates. Notable examples of such creatures include the[i] laloumena[/i], for which one of the other hippo species is named and which is also the Malagasy word for hippo, and the [i]kilopilopitsofy[/i], which inspired the appearance of this version as it was described as dark-colored and having floppy ears. The hippos in this mod produce baobab fruit in the summer.[/*]
[*]The [b]Warrah[/b] ([i]Dusicyon australis[/i]), also called the Falkland Islands Wolf, was the only native land animal of the Falkland Islands in the southern Atlantic. Its closest living relative is the maned wolf. Going extinct in the 1870s, Charles Darwin described the warrah in his journals some 40 years before and feared for its extinction then; though naturally unafraid of humans, it was eradicated as settlers on the islands considered it a threat to their sheep. This version produces foxberries, a native plant of the islands, in winter.[/*]
[/list]At the time of my updating this we're at over 28,000 unique downloads! Thank you all for your support, I never expected this mod to be so popular. To celebrate I've added a new addition to the pack
[list]
[*]The Mediterranean was home to many different dwarf elephant species, and the [b]Tilos Dwarf Elephant[/b] ([i]Paleoloxodon tiliensis[/i]) was the last surviving of these, going extinct between 4,000 and 1,500 BCE. With an average height of 5'1" and a maximum height of 6'2", it was relatively large for a dwarf elephant. Unlike the other animals in this mod, their extinction was most likely not the work of humans and instead was most likely caused by the eruption of one of the nearby volcanoes. Its closest modern relative is the critically endangered African Forest Elephant, [i]Loxodonta cyclotis[/i]. These elephants will produce smyrna figs in the fall, and silphium (a likely extinct relative of giant fennel, prized in ancient times for a variety of uses), in the summer at high friendship. They come in two possible colors, inspired by the Amazonian Manatee and Black & Rufous Sengi respectively.[/*]
[/list]Note that the elephant is meant to be a somewhat more challenging animal than the others in the pack. To unlock it, you must first catch a lava eel; being elephants they are expensive, and take a whole season to hit maturity.

Take these reconstructions with a grain of salt (especially Chendytes, as I couldn't find any images of actual fossils), and enjoy!
